earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists and classification checklists (Laycock 1973; Haberland 1963); no descriptive phonology exists.

sources.citation: Bruce, Les. 1984. The Alamblak language of Papua New Guinea (East Sepik). Pacific Linguistics C-81.
sources.note: Published version of Bruce 1979; only relevant as the best-described Sepik Hill relative (Alamblak stress rules), not for Mari itself. Open at ANU (handle 1885/145229).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mari language (Sepik)' (accessed 2026-09-17; cites Ethnologue 25th ed. and Global Recordings Network).
sources.note: Nothing; ~80 speakers, Mari village, Gawi Rural LLG; GRN audio recordings exist.

sources.citation: Sumbuk, Kenneth Memson. 1999. Morphosyntax of Sare. PhD thesis, University of Waikato. xiii+335 pp. (hdl 10289/13888). Ch.1 with Chart 1.1 'The position of Sare within the Sepik area Papuan languages (Laycock 1973)'; 2.2.1 Stress (pp.40-42) for Sare/Kapriman only.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Read held by the project: the thesis describes Sare (Kapriman, kapr1245) only; p.2 'Of the Sepik Hill Family, to which Sare belongs, only Alamblak (Bruce 1984), has a comprehensive description'; the explicit stress rule (2.2.1, pp.40-42: secondary stress initial, primary stress final in disyllables and penultimate in longer words) is for Sare alone; nothing on this language.

sources.citation: Toyoda, Yukio. 1998. To which bird do you belong?: Totemic belief among the Mari, Papua New Guinea. In: Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea (Senri Ethnological Studies 47, ed. S. Yoshida & Y. Toyoda), 61-77. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology. DOI 10.15021/00002911; hdl 10502/843.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or prosody. The only linguistic remarks: the classification sentence (p. 65), 'the people of the Yembiyembi, Menchuat and Changriman.. speak a very similar language to theirs, and the Mari roughly understand their language' (p. 65), and note 6 (p. 76): 'The orthography of the Mari language has not been established, and the transcription in this paper is made only for temporary use.' A handful of Mari words are transcribed without stress marks (village names Mosim, Murim; lineage totems yaada 'parakeet', dos[i] 'crowned pigeon', etc.). Fieldwork July-September 1988 (note 1…

sources.citation: Yoshida, Shuji & Yukio Toyoda (eds.). 1998. Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea. Senri Ethnological Studies 47. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology. Chapters: Toyoda, Introduction: Fringe area of Highlands in PNG (1-20); Yamada, Sound of bamboo as talk of spirit.. Waxei (21-41); Kumagai, Migration and shifting settlement patterns among the Kapriman (43-60); Toyoda, To which bird do you belong? Totemic belief among the Mari (61-77; doi:10.15021/00002911); Kawasaki, Pigs, two women and an island.. Bahinemo mythology (79-91); Saito, We are one flesh: unity and migration of the Yabio (93-112); Yoshida, Numeral classifiers among the May River Iwam (113-138); Kurita (Fasu), Akimichi (Seltaman/Gidra).
sources.note: Ethnographic; no phonology. States only the classification, that Yembiyembi/Menchuat/Changriman (= Bisis villages) 'speak a very similar language.. and the Mari roughly understand their language' (p.65), and n.6: 'The orthography of the Mari language has not been established, and the transcription in this paper is made only for temporary use.' Mari totem/kin terms are cited without stress or tone marks.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (Language index entry 'Mari (E Sepik, S of Chambri)'.)
sources.note: No phonology content (bibliography). The Mari entry lists only Voegelin & Voegelin 1965 and Wurm & Hattori 1981 (classification/atlas); the 'Sepik Hill languages' entry lists Dye & Townsend 1968, Hatanaka & Bragge 1973, Sanders 1977, W&H 1981. Confirms that through 1995 no description, sketch, survey report or catalogued SIL manuscript specific to Mari existed (Dye's 1967 wordlist is not indexed).

sources.citation: Laycock, Don. 1991. Three vowels, semivowels, and neutralisation: orthographic and other problems of Sepik languages. PL A-73: 107-114.
sources.note: Does not mention Mari; general Sepik vowel/orthography discussion only.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (PL A-76): 243-274, section 4.2 Sepik Hill Stock/Family.
sources.note: Nothing; Mari is only listed among Sepik Hill languages (Bruce 1979 / Wurm 1982 subgroupings).

sources.citation: 吉田集而 [Yoshida, Shuji] (PI) et al. 1988-1989. パプアニューギニア、セピック丘陵における文化人類学的研究 [Cultural-anthropological research in the Sepik Hills, Papua New Guinea]. KAKENHI project 63041138 (National Museum of Ethnology), research-result summaries; and 斉藤尚文 (PI) et al. 2002-2004, パプアニューギニア、セピック丘陵地域における開発的介入とその現地社会への影響, KAKENHI project 14401016.
sources.note: summary only; no linguistic content

sources.citation: Bruce, Leslie P., Jr. 1979. A grammar of Alamblak (Papua New Guinea). PhD thesis, Australian National University. pp. 23-24 (data sources) and comparative Sepik Hill chapter pp. 472-519.
sources.note: Stress-placement rules (ch. on phonology, pp. ~97ff.) are for Alamblak only. Mari enters only as comparative wordlist data taken from Dye et al. 1968 ('the data for six languages consist of word lists collected by Dye, et al. (1968). These languages are Kaningara, Kapriman-Karambit, Watakataui, Bisis, Mari, and Bitara'); no statement about Mari stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page mari1432 (subclassification refs Bruce 1979: 472-519; Haberland & Seyfarth 1974: 24; AES status shifting; links to Ethnologue, OLAC, ELP).
sources.note: Nothing; no descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) reference is listed for the language — only overview/wordlist/classification items.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Only a phylum-level typological checklist (p. 732) whose features 'are found in a majority of the languages': low vowel inventories, quasi-phonemic schwa, palatal series, plain vs prenasalised stops, and 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems'; tone is discussed only for Upper Sepik languages (Abau, Iwam, Wogamusin, p. 744-745). The Sepik Hill Family section 2.11.3.1.3.4 (p. 752) is classificatory (documented by Dye & Townsends 1969; SIL teams in Alamblak, Bahinemo, Sanio, Hewa; 'very few publications') with no phonology. Nothing on Mari stress or tone.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. Entry 101 MARI, p. 29 (p. 33).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives only village (Mari, CD 44E), population (120) and a comment that Dye & Townsends' figure of 147 suggests uncensused hamlets; no linguistic data at all.

sources.citation: Dye, Wayne, Patricia Townsend & William Townsend. 1969 [1968]. The Sepik Hill languages: a preliminary report. Oceania 39(2): 146-156.
sources.note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Mari; this work adds nothing on stress either. It only establishes the language (147 speakers, Mari Lake / Salumei River, Sepik Hill Family, 45% cognates with Bahinemo) and explicitly says the survey data were insufficient for phonemicization and that phonological description remains to be done.

sources.citation: Dye, Wayne. 1967. Mari word list. Unpublished SIL survey word list, held by the project at SIL, Ukarumpa (PNG). Attested as the source of ASJP wordlist MARI_PNG_2 (compiled by Matthew S. Dryer), The ASJP Database (Wichmann, Brown, Holman, Dryer & Ran eds.).
sources.note: ASJP 40-item list in ASJPcode with no stress or tone marking (ASJP orthography discards suprasegmentals); a second ASJP list MARI_PNG (source Haberland 1963 ms.) has only numerals 'd3bais' one, 'woti' two. Wordlist-only data, no statement.
